policy.purpose: Record AMD hardware acceleration opportunities or AGS parity contracts that were actively investigated for APUSR but cannot currently be represented faithfully through the shader-facing DXC/DXIL/SPIR-V contracts used by the project.
policy.rule: A blocker is not an implementation. Do not replace it with generic arithmetic, ordinary loads/stores, synchronization, guessed indexing, or weaker ordering semantics merely to mark the row complete.
policy.qualification: A blocker counts as attempted for integration-branch readiness only when the missing ingress or semantic proof and the required real fix are explicit.

blockers.dxil: No shader-facing HLSL/DXIL intrinsic in this DXC fork that preserves AMD async global-to-LDS intent.
blockers.spirv: No currently used core/KHR/AMD SPIR-V instruction in the branch that carries the AMD async global-to-LDS operation as such.
blockers.required_fix: Add a real shader/IR contract that can preserve the asynchronous transfer and synchronization semantics through the backend; do not substitute an ordinary load plus groupshared store.

blockers.dxil: No shader-facing AMD async LDS-to-global contract identified.
blockers.spirv: No exact SPIR-V ingress identified for the AMD async store operation.
blockers.required_fix: Expose an exact asynchronous transfer contract or an AMD SPIR-V extension/backend-recognition path; ordinary workgroup load plus global store is not equivalent.

blockers.dxil: No direct shader-facing DXIL contract identified for AMD transposed-load intent.
blockers.spirv: Generic vector/scalar loads express values but not the hardware transposed-load operation or layout intent.
blockers.required_fix: Add a layout-aware intrinsic/IR contract or prove a canonical load graph is reliably recognized by the Radeon backend before calling this supported.

blockers.dxil: DXC has generic LLVM prefetch machinery for CPU-oriented targets but no HLSL/DXIL shader contract that preserves AMD GPU prefetch intent.
blockers.spirv: No exact shader prefetch operation is available in the branch's Vulkan contract surface.
blockers.required_fix: Introduce a shader-visible prefetch contract with defined cache/scope semantics or an AMD-specific extension; do not model prefetch as a value-producing load.

blockers.dxil: No shader-facing contract identified that denotes the AMD async transaction group being waited on.
blockers.spirv: Ordinary memory barriers do not identify or preserve the AMD async transfer dependency represented by these intrinsics.
blockers.required_fix: Pair a first-class async-transfer ingress with a matching wait/dependency primitive.

blockers.dxil: No HLSL/DXIL contract identified for AMD scheduler grouping hints.
blockers.spirv: No portable SPIR-V semantic operation corresponds to an AMD backend scheduling hint.
blockers.required_fix: Use an AMD-specific compiler option/metadata/intrinsic path that survives to the Radeon backend; this is not representable as a memory barrier.

blockers.dxil: Ordinary scalar/vector DXIL still has no first-class BF16 arithmetic type. SM 6.10 LinAlg BF16 is a separate matrix contract.
blockers.spirv: The branch now has genuine BFloat16KHR scalar/vector types and OpFConvert conversion ingress. BF16->F32 is exact. Vulkan does not define one universal F32->BF16 narrowing result, and SPIR-V has no seed-carrying stochastic-rounding BF16 conversion equivalent to AMD's cvt_sr forms.
blockers.required_fix: Use a Vulkan/SPIR-V contract that pins the required F32->BF16 rounding mode when bit-exact narrowing matters, and add a real seed-carrying intrinsic/extension for AMD stochastic-rounding conversion. Do not implement either as integer bit arithmetic and call it native.

apusr_relevance: raw/stateless GPU-address access, packed metadata and future persistent/tiled kernels
blockers.dxil: AGS defines a 64-bit GPU VA plus a separate 32-bit offset and native raw load.
blockers.spirv: DXC can express a physical-storage-buffer RawBufferLoad from a 64-bit device address, but the public AGS header does not specify whether its offset is byte-scaled or DWORD-scaled and no authoritative public call site was found.
blockers.required_fix: Run a tiny DX12 differential test over offsets 1, 2 and 4 against known memory, then encode the proven scaling in the Vulkan physical-address helper. Do not guess address+offset versus address+4*offset.

apusr_relevance: future packed metadata and global synchronization structures requiring true 64-bit raw atomics
blockers.dxil: DXIL has native 64-bit ByteAddressBuffer atomic operations.
blockers.spirv: The current SPIR-V backend represents RWByteAddressBuffer as 32-bit uint words. Its raw atomic handler constructs a 32-bit pointee and cannot faithfully issue one 64-bit atomic operation; most *64 methods fail as unimplemented, while Min64/Max64 route toward that 32-bit handler and therefore are not claimed supported.
blockers.required_fix: Introduce a legal 8-byte-aligned 64-bit raw-buffer pointee/alias representation that can feed Int64Atomics, then qualify every operation and Min/Max signedness. Never split one 64-bit atomic into two 32-bit atomics.

apusr_relevance: FP16 packing, quantization boundaries and deterministic conversion paths
blockers.dxil: AGS provides all three modes and returns the resulting F16 encoding as a value.
blockers.spirv: SPIR-V FPRoundingMode can request RTE/RTN/RTP on OpFConvert, but Vulkan restricts the decorated narrowing conversion to specific direct-store uses. That does not represent AGS's reusable returned F16-bit value contract. Standard f32tof16 covers nearest-even only.
blockers.required_fix: Use a future Vulkan/SPIR-V value-producing directional half-conversion contract or a real AMD extension/backend intrinsic. Software bit emulation is not accepted as native parity.

apusr_relevance: shader microbenchmarking and precise qualification instrumentation
blockers.dxil: AGS defines a globally coherent realtime clock read that also acts as a code-motion barrier.
blockers.spirv: Device-scope OpReadClockKHR supplies a device-consistent clock value, but SPV_KHR_shader_clock explicitly does not promise a code-motion barrier.
blockers.required_fix: Add a barrier-preserving AMD/compiler intrinsic or extension. DeviceClockNoBarrier remains qualification instrumentation only and must not be labeled ShaderRealtimeClock parity.

apusr_relevance: low priority; modern APUSR math paths do not require legacy behavior
blockers.dxil: Ordinary HLSL arithmetic is not semantically equivalent to the legacy/assist operations.
blockers.spirv: No exact ingress established for the AMD legacy/assist semantics.
blockers.required_fix: Only add if a real APUSR consumer appears or a native AMD extension/contract is introduced; do not relabel standard arithmetic as the legacy operation.
